detail.title: Intelligent Disobedience Modeling
detail.question: How can intelligent agents be mathematically modeled to perform 'intelligent disobedience' in safety-critical shared autonomy?
detail.reason: The provided source arXiv:2603.20994 introduces a specific game-theoretic framework relevant to our topic of obedience limits.

detail.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via IDG
detail.summary: The Intelligent Disobedience Game (IDG) models interactions between a human leader and an assistive follower as a Stackelberg game. It defines 'intelligent disobedience' as the agent's decision to override human instructions to prevent harm, a necessary evolution from simple compliance. The model identifies 'safety traps' where an agent avoids harm but fails to achieve the human's goal, providing a testbed for learning safe non-compliance.
detail.reason: To synthesize the initial formalization of intelligent disobedience and address the project objective.
